slices.focus: Colleen prepares to present the school program to the museum board as a growth case, marking its transition from personal crusade to institutional initiative.
slices.summary: Colleen compiles a full school year with bookings spread across fall, winter, and spring; a wider mix of district and charter schools; and proof that trained volunteers can deliver repeat visits. Leonard agrees this should be a board growth case, not a side update. She structures the presentation around three claims (year-round demand, broader school reach, non-person-dependent delivery) and prepares boundary sentences about what she will and won't absorb without support. She names the shift: from advocate to witness.
open_loops: Trim overcrowded chart from deck before presentation
Prepare two boundary sentences: what to build next (stable repeat scheduling) and what not to absorb (automatic solution for every imagined extra)
Save one paragraph for herself after, separate from the presentation
decisions: Colleen's school program is now substantial enough to be presented to the museum board with year-round booking metrics,
Colleen feels proud and relieved that the school program has moved from a personal crusade to something the institution
